planting.note: Plant tubers shallowly in sharply drained, humus-rich soil in shade; Crete cyclamen needs a hot, bone-dry summer dormancy and is reliably hardy outdoors only from zone 9 southward.

directions: Plant tubers shallowly in sharply drained, humus-rich soil in shade; Crete cyclamen bears pure white, sweetly fragrant, elegantly tapered flowers from late winter into spring above silver-marbled, heart-shaped leaves. It is among the most cold-tender of the garden cyclamen, reliable outdoors only in zone 9 and warmer, and is best grown in a pot in an alpine house or cold frame where winters are colder. Keep it bone dry through its hot, dry summer dormancy, since excess moisture then is the chief cause of tuber rot.

planting.note: Plant the tiny tubers shallowly in gritty, sharply drained soil in shade to part shade; this diminutive Turkish species does best in a trough, pot, or alpine garden kept free of summer moisture.

directions: Plant the tiny tubers shallowly in gritty, sharply drained soil in shade or part shade, where this diminutive Turkish species performs best as a container or alpine-garden plant kept free of summer moisture. Cyclamen intaminatum produces small, nearly round, silver-marbled leaves and dainty white to pale pink flowers lacking the dark nose typical of most cyclamen, blooming from late summer into autumn. Though reasonably frost-hardy, its small stature makes it easily swamped by larger neighbors, so give it its own well-drained spot rather than a crowded bed.

planting.note: Plant tubers in cool, humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil in a partly shaded site; this alpine species has no true dry summer dormancy and resents the hot, parched conditions that suit most other hardy cyclamen.

directions: Plant tubers in humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil in a cool, partly shaded site, since this diminutive alpine species from Turkey's Pontic Mountains comes from high-elevation turf with heavy snow cover and ample summer moisture, unlike the dry-summer habit of most other hardy cyclamen. It bears small, plain green, largely unmarked leaves that persist nearly year-round and tiny, blue-pink, faintly scented flowers with a purple basal zone in spring as the snow melts. As the smallest and one of the hardiest cyclamen species, it suits a cool rock garden, trough, or alpine house rather than a hot, dry border.

planting.note: Plant tubers in sharply drained, limestone-based soil in deep shade; Balearic cyclamen tolerates a light overnight frost but not sustained hard freezes.

directions: Plant tubers in sharply drained, limestone-based soil in deep shade beneath evergreen oak or pine, mimicking the shady, north-facing slopes and rock crevices of its native Balearic Islands and southern France. It produces blue-green, silver-marbled leaves and sweetly fragrant, pale pink-to-white flowers from late winter into spring. It tolerates a light overnight frost but not sustained hard freezes, so where winters run colder than zone 8 it is best grown as a container plant in a cool greenhouse.

planting.note: Plant tubers in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shady woodland or at the base of rocky outcrops; give it a dry summer rest once the foliage dies down.

directions: Plant tubers in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shady woodland, scrub, or at the base of cliffs, replicating the humid but sharply draining sites of its native Peloponnese and nearby Greek islands. Closely related to Cyclamen repandum, it bears broad, silver-splashed leaves and narrow-petaled, pale-to-deep pink flowers with a darker pink nose in spring. Give it a dry summer rest once the foliage dies down, and protect it from prolonged hard freezes in the colder parts of its hardiness range.

common_name: Propeller Cyclamen (Turkish Alpine Cyclamen, syn. Cyclamen trochopteranthum)

planting.note: Plant tubers shallowly in gritty, sharply drained soil in dry shade; this coum relative needs a dry summer dormancy and resents waterlogged winter soil far more than cold alone.

directions: Plant tubers shallowly in gritty, sharply drained soil in dry shade, where this close relative of Cyclamen coum (long sold in the trade as Cyclamen trochopteranthum) produces rounded, silver-marbled leaves and honey-scented flowers from late summer into winter. Its most distinctive feature is the unusual propeller-like shape of the flowers, caused by petals reflexed only about 90 degrees and slightly twisted rather than fully swept back. Keep it dry through summer dormancy and site it where winter wet drains away quickly, since soggy soil troubles it far more than cold alone.

common_name: Maurice Dryden Cyclamen (Silver Pewter-Leaf Winter Cyclamen)

planting.note: Plant tubers shallowly in humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in partial to full shade, as for typical Cyclamen coum.

directions: Plant tubers shallowly in humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in partial to full shade; 'Maurice Dryden' is a prized named selection of winter cyclamen with rounded leaves clouded almost entirely in silvery pewter and edged with a narrow green border, among the most striking foliage of any hardy cyclamen cultivar. Clean white flowers with a dark plum-purple nose appear in abundance just above the leaves from January into March. Because the silver leaf pattern is a selected clonal trait, propagate by division or purchase named stock rather than relying on open-pollinated seed, which will not come true.

planting.note: Plant tubers 1-2 inches deep in well-drained, humus-rich, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in partial to full shade, exactly as for typical Cyclamen coum.

directions: Plant tubers 1-2 inches deep in well-drained, humus-rich, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in partial to full shade, exactly as for typical Cyclamen coum. This rare natural forma lacks the dark basal stain found in almost all other coum forms, producing clean, unmarked pure white flowers from January into March above rounded, variably marbled leaves. Because pure white seedlings are uncommon even among albissimum-type plants, grow it isolated from pink-flowered cyclamen if collecting your own seed, so the pure white strain comes true.
